test_focus: N=30 confirmation of engineering-craft seeds > computing-history seeds on the two DECISION-shaped technical scenarios where the effect was strongest in Phase 15 (62.9% EC win, N=70) and Phase 16 (87% and 60% EC per-scenario at N=15).
tester: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context), live as the developer

experiment_design.scenario_selection: legacy-deletion + refactor-decision — the two decision-shaped scenarios from Phase 14 (55% and 25% treatment-win baselines) where Phase 15+16 saw the strongest EC>CH effect
arms: engineering-craft (EC) — 5-dream archive with day-to-day-craft texture (the bug live for six years, the feature flag from 2017)
computing-history (CH) — 5-dream archive with historical-figure texture (Hamilton, Knuth, Engelbart, Hopper, Thompson)
experiment_design.judge_design: Direct EC-vs-CH head-to-head. Both arms use the neutral wrapper. Response order randomized per trial.

aggregate.interpretation: EC wins 66.7% of head-to-heads on decision-shaped scenarios at N=60. 95% CI [54.1%, 77.3%] EXCLUDES 50% — statistically significant content-routing effect.

per_scenario.comparison: Phase 16 N=15: EC 87% [62%, 96%] — Phase 20 N=30: 60% [42%, 75%]. The Phase 16 magnitude regressed toward 60%; CIs heavily overlap. Both runs find EC>CH directionally.
Phase 16 N=15: EC 60% [36%, 80%] — Phase 20 N=30: 73% [56%, 86%]. The effect strengthened with more data; CIs overlap but Phase 20 is tighter.

implications: **EC > CH on decision-shaped scenarios is REAL.** At N=60 the lower CI bound is 54%, above 50%. Phase 15's 63% directional finding is confirmed at higher N.

**Phase 16's aggregate 'EC and CH are tied' result is explained by per-scenario heterogeneity.** When EC dominates on 2 scenarios (legacy-deletion, refactor-decision) and CH dominates on 2-3 others (slow-prod-query, retry-under-load, memory-creep), the aggregate is ~tied. The signal washes out in the average.

**Content routing is justified specifically for decision-shaped technical work.** An engineering agent answering 'which approach should I take?' or 'what's the right way to be sure?' benefits from engineering-craft seeds (the texture of 'I've seen this before — the system has hidden context') over historical-figure seeds.

**The shipping engineering preference order (engineering-craft FIRST) is now justified beyond Phase 15.** The first commit to use it (Phase 15 + later) had reasonable data; this phase confirms it with proper statistical power on the strongest-effect subset.

**Future content-routing per-prompt** (Phase 21 suggested) could surface the EC advantage on decision-shaped prompts while letting CH (or a broader mix) handle pure-debugging prompts. The Phase 16 per-scenario heterogeneity is the design rationale.
**Phase 15 magnitude (62.9%) lands within Phase 20's CI [54.1%, 77.3%].** The Phase 15 result was real, just at the noisier end.

feature_verdicts.shipping_engineering_preference_order: justified by data, not just intuition
feature_verdicts.per_scenario_heterogeneity_pattern: confirmed — decision-shaped scenarios favor EC, debugging-shaped scenarios are closer or favor CH

known_limitations: Two scenarios is a small base for the 'decision-shaped class.' A future phase could expand to 4-5 decision-shaped scenarios.
The result is conditional on the neutral wrapper. We didn't re-test EC vs CH with the dreams wrapper at N=60.
The aggregate effect-size estimate (66.7%) is the average of scenario-level rates (60% and 73%). Real production with a different mix of decision-shaped prompts would have a different average.
verdict: STATISTICALLY ROBUST WIN — engineering-craft seeds beat computing-history seeds on decision-shaped technical scenarios. The shipping content preferences are justified beyond noise.
next_steps: Phase 21 (suggested): per-prompt CONTENT routing. Route the seed archive per-prompt based on classify_prompt_domain (decision vs. debugging) rather than per-agent. The per-scenario heterogeneity from Phase 16 + Phase 20 makes this the highest-leverage next refinement.

Phase 24 (suggested): expand the 'decision-shaped' scenario class to 4-5 prompts and re-confirm the EC effect at N=30+ across all of them. The Phase 20 result is solid at N=60 but built on 2 scenario archetypes.
